1.say: Check that. That describes metabolism. What does homeostasis keep stable?
hit: homeostasis is all the chemical reactions in the body
miss: Homeostasis is keeping a stable internal environment, even when conditions outside change
homeostasis is keeping the inside steady even if the outside changes
homeostasis is not metabolism it is keeping a stable internal environment

3.say: Check that. Do plants and bacteria have that? Is it one of the 8?
hit: all living things have a brain and are made of cells
living things need blood and use energy
miss: Made of cells, has a universal genetic code (DNA), grows and develops, reproduces, responds to the environment, maintains homeostasis, uses energy (metabolism), and evolves as a group
living things are made of cells use energy grow and reproduce
not all living things have a brain but all are made of cells
living things dont need a heart but they respond to the environment

4.say: Check that. Body systems work together. How does one system help another?
hit: each body system works alone to keep homeostasis
the systems work separately the lungs get oxygen and the heart pumps
miss: The respiratory system brings in oxygen, and the circulatory system carries it to the cells. The digestive system breaks food into nutrients, and the circulatory system delivers them. The nervous system senses changes and signals muscles or glands to respond.
body systems do not work alone they work together
no system works by itself the respiratory and circulatory systems work together

7.say: Check that. Is that food rich in protein, or in a different nutrient?
hit: examples of proteins are bread and pasta
proteins build muscle like butter and oil
miss: Proteins build and repair the body, act as enzymes that control the rates of reactions, and transport substances. Their monomer is the amino acid. Examples: meat, eggs, beans
examples meat eggs beans and fish
foods like peanut butter and chicken have protein
proteins build and repair muscles examples are steak and nuts

8.say: Check that. Which organ absorbs most of the nutrients?
hit: the large intestine absorbs most nutrients into the blood
after the stomach nutrients are absorbed in the large intestine
miss: Mouth: teeth chew food (mechanical) and amylase in saliva starts digesting starch. Stomach: churns food and pepsin starts digesting protein, making chyme. Small intestine: finishes chemical digestion and absorbs most nutrients into the blood
small intestine finishes digestion and absorbs nutrients into the blood
the small intestine absorbs nutrients and the large intestine absorbs water
the large intestine absorbs water not most nutrients

15.say: Check that. Arteries carry high-pressure blood. What are their walls like?
hit: arteries have thin walls so blood flows easily
arteries carry low pressure blood away from the heart
miss: Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure, so they have thick, elastic walls. Veins carry low-pressure blood back to the heart, so they have valves to keep it from flowing backward. Capillaries have walls one cell thick so oxygen and nutrients can pass into the cells.
arteries have thick elastic walls because of high pressure
arteries are not thin they are thick and stretchy
capillaries are thin and arteries are thick

17.say: Check that. The alveoli are the last stop. What comes before them?
hit: nose pharynx larynx trachea alveoli bronchi
miss: Nose, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli
air goes nose pharynx larynx trachea bronchi bronchioles and ends at the alveoli
nose to throat to trachea to bronchi to bronchioles to alveoli

20.say: Check that. Which part of the brain controls breathing rate?
hit: when co2 rises the cerebellum makes you breathe faster
the cerebrum tells you to breathe faster when carbon dioxide goes up
miss: The respiratory system brings oxygen into the lungs, and the circulatory system carries it to the cells. The blood carries carbon dioxide back to the lungs to be breathed out. When carbon dioxide rises, the medulla oblongata makes you breathe faster
the medulla oblongata senses carbon dioxide and makes you breathe faster
the brain stem makes you breathe faster when co2 goes up
